limits: Terminology substitution is not encryption, general secret redaction or OS isolation.
Per-file operations require existing parent directories; reads are bounded and remembered hashes are limited to 256 paths.
The configured mapping is fixed for the server lifetime; reconnects require a new read or the earlier source hash.
Hash rechecks and the server lock do not provide atomic compare-and-swap against unrelated racing writers.
Profanity matches are lexical and limited to the selected vocabulary; they do not infer intent, stem words, or normalize arbitrary disguises/languages.
Operator scan output contains matched original terms and is not exposed by the dedicated agent server.
Case markers require v0.4.3+; old saved dictionaries and literal markers remain supported.
Project export creates selected directory structure; the separate direct agent file interface still requires existing parents.
Project snapshots and original/reverse mappings remain private outside the view, but a view directory is context separation rather than OS isolation.
Imports are recoverable multi-file publications, not atomic transactions against unrelated writers. Explicit recovery requires unchanged retained view bytes and compatible source state.
A completed view is consumed; later source/view drift is reported separately from its historical completion receipt.
No external agent/model acceptance, remote CI, host isolation or whole-project completeness is claimed.
Markdown uses CommonMark with conservative full-link protection; Markdown parsing is bounded to 1000000 characters. Additional dialects/source-code refactoring are not claimed.

JSON translates only explicit exact string-value pointers. Changed selected tokens may normalize JSON escaping; unchanged selected tokens use private context for exact original spelling. Unselected bytes stay unchanged.
Document rules require product 0.4.5 for new v2 ledgers/policies; old v1 ledgers/views remain supported and retained 0.4.4 view receipts were inspected read-only with the new code.
The direct source-agent MCP retains whole-term text behavior; Vandal routes mixed structured work through version-2 neutral project views.
Vandal 0.2 is a repository-specific workflow, independently versioned from Bamboozle 0.4.5. Its helper generates configurations and does not install, register or launch clients.
Syntax protection is not secret redaction. Supplied fixtures, explicit copied content, OS isolation, model behavior, schema generation and broader language adapters remain separate responsibilities.
